notes: Intro call 2025-09-10 – heavy interest in deterministic tail-latency for agent assist during campaign spikes. 'If response times jump, agents fallback to manual — unacceptable.'
Primary workload: live agent assist (real-time suggestions), post-chat ticket summarization, and automated tool-calling to CRM/billing systems.
SLO targets: p95 < 300ms for short assistant responses; worried about p99 tail during 10–20x spikes. Baseline 750 req/min; planning for peak 15k req/min, seasonal up to 20x baseline (BFCM).

Technical asks: predictable tail-latency, transparent per-token cost, model routing with graceful fallback (quantized variants), persistent KV/prefix cache across agent sessions, and circuit-breaker for external tool-calls.
Operational constraints: must integrate with existing ACD & telephony routing, maintain audit logs, and meet EU data residency for EU customers. Prefer VPC/private control plane for PII routes.
Tool-calling risk: external API rate limits amplify queueing — Elmbridge needs builtin retry/backpressure hooks and explicit retry budget visibility.
Cost: open to Dedicated reserved capacity if predictable TCO; wants delta analysis (Dedicated vs Hosted with burst capacity) and options for autoscale + burst pools.
Model preference: open-family models with validated hallucination profiles; acceptable to route to smaller verified models for non-critical summarization to save cost.
Security note: security team flagged DLP/KMS questions — must confirm HSM/KMS integration and retention controls before procurement.
CTO quote: 'We need a plan for our holiday spike — cannot have >2% SLA drift under 10x load.'
